newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. debt futures finish pit trading weaker.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. debt futures finish pit trading weaker.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended pit trading weaker, with most units clinging near session price troughs during a quiet afternoon.
Action in the long and intermediate ends stayed subdued, with turnover picking up slightly before June Treasury bond and note futures-options went off the boards at midday.
Although traders noted some two-way options flows during the last few minutes of bond options trade, they said the expiration proceeded relatively uneventfully.
"It was not very exciting," said one options broker. "We had some play both ways."
"It's (expiration) been controlled, really quiet," said another options broker.
"We really didn't seen any activity," said a third broker.
Some said late speculative plays with out-of-the-money options, including 112 calls and 106 puts, helped pressure June T-bond futures to the day's low just before noon.
But others pooh-poohed that idea and instead tied the slippage to talk that a large hedge fund was selling futures.
"I think that would be stretching it to link the two," said the third broker of the late options plays and the dip in June T-bonds to 109-27/32.
Brokers agreed the market could stay stuck until it divines whether the Federal Open Market Committee Tuesday will jack up domestic interest rates another notch.
"It's (market) just sitting here," said the third broker. "If you think this is bad, wait until Monday."
"I think we're stuck until Tuesday," said the first broker.
Although the market generally appeared divided over whether the Fed will tighten or not, the three options brokers all said they expected a 25-basis-point increase.
"I think they will hike," the first added.
"I think they will hike," he added. "When in doubt, look for the one (action) that's going to cause the most damage, and I think they will (tighten)."

June T-bonds also backed down again from resistance near Friday's overall price peak at 110-16/32, which it brushed hit in overnight electronic trading and which brokers said roughly equalled support in the cash yield of around 6.87 percent.

Futures wobbled slightly when April U.S. housing starts rose 2.6 percent to an annualized rate of 1.473 million units. Traders had forecasts starts rising 0.4 percent to 1.43 million units from the original March rate of 1.425 million.
April permits fell 0.8 percent to 1.46 million. March starts and permits were revised upward.

The stronger-than-expected rise in the University of Michigan preliminary May consumer sentiment index to 104.6 against forecasts for 101.6 had a more muted effect on expiration Friday and before Tuesday, brokers said.

June T-bonds settled down 11/32 at 109-31/32, T-notes eased 5/32 to 107-09/32, muni-bonds rose 3/32 to 116-13/32, Sept T-bills fell 0.030 to 94.500, and December Eurodollars lost 0.025 to 93.690. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
